recommendations.text: Investigate the cart and invoice calculation paths and identify the cause of the reported one-cent discrepancy, including where discount application, tax calculation, precision, or rounding diverges.

Read docs/MONEY.md and use its rules as the authoritative monetary calculation contract. Make cart totals and printed invoice totals comply with those rules for every order, not only the reported example.

Ensure equivalent order inputs produce identical cart and invoice totals. Prefer a shared calculation implementation, or otherwise enforce the same documented calculation and rounding rules across both paths.

Add a regression test for three items priced at 0.35 each with a 15% member discount and 20% tax. Derive the expected total independently from docs/MONEY.md and verify both checkout and printed invoice output against it.

Add regression coverage for rounding boundaries and relevant supported order variations identified during investigation, asserting both agreement between cart and invoice and compliance with docs/MONEY.md.
Run the regression tests and the repository's configured test suite using npm test; report results and any remaining failures.

The supplied evidence contains neither docs/MONEY.md nor calculation code, so the root cause, rounding contract, and correct example total remain unverified. Do not assume a rounding mode or discount/tax ordering before inspecting them.

ambiguities: Does “for every order” include recalculating or reissuing invoices already finalized, or only ensuring correct calculations for orders processed after the fix?

spec.rawIntent: Customers report that the total printed on an invoice sometimes differs by a cent from the total the cart showed at checkout, for example three items at 0.35 with the 15% member discount and 20% tax. Find out why the cart and the invoice disagree, make both follow the rules in docs/MONEY.md for every order, and add regression tests.
